questions.text: What is the register map of the test shell (offset, width, reset value and access of every register: byte in, tick, status, reply length, reply index and data, telemetry length, index, data, take)?
questions.default: The map in registers.map: 0x00 ID, 0x04 BYTE_IN, 0x08 TICK, 0x0C STATUS, 0x10 REPLY_LEN, 0x14 REPLY_IDX, 0x18 REPLY_DATA, 0x1C TELEM_LEN, 0x20 TELEM_IDX, 0x24 TELEM_DATA, 0x28 TELEM_TAKE, all 32 bits wide
questions.reason: The request names these registers but gives no offsets.
questions.answer:
IN: offset 0x00, WO, reset 0: [7:0] packet byte, [8] end flag
STAT: offset 0x09, RO, reset 0: [0] telemetry on, [1] busy
RIDX: offset 0x03, RW, reset 0: [6:0] word number
RWORD: offset 0x04, RO, reset 0: bytes 4i..4i+3 of the reply, first byte on top, zero past the end
RLEN: offset 0x02, RO, reset 0: length in bytes of the latest reply, 0 if none
TICK: offset 0x01, WO, reset 0: [7:0] n ticks
TIDX: offset 0x06, RW, reset 0: [6:0] word number
TWORD: offset 0x07, RO, reset 0: same for the telemetry frame
TAKE: offset 0x08, WO, reset 0: any write takes the held telemetry frame
TLEN: offset 0x05, RO, reset 0: length of the held telemetry frame, 0 if none
shell: test shell, PROTOCOL.md 1.1
unmapped: no register at an offset: reads 0, writes ignored (read-only registers behave the same on write)
questions.evidence: IN: offset 0x00, WO, reset 0: [7:0] packet byte, [8] end flag

questions.text: Which counter takes a wrong register number combined with a write to a read-only register, and does an unknown register get the type/length/register/access counter?
questions.default: Both go to the type, length, register or access error counter (the seventh).
questions.reason: The status layout lists a single counter for these.
questions.answer: Both go to the type, length, register or access error counter (the seventh).

questions.text: Is a packet with a bad type or wrong length counted as using up its sequence number?
questions.default: No: those rules come before the sequence rule, so the number is not used up.
questions.reason: Judging order puts them before the sequence rule.
questions.answer: No. A packet that fails the type or length check is refused before the sequence rule, so it never passes that rule and does not use up its sequence number.
questions.evidence: Checks in order: long, short, bad CRC (silent drops), type, length, sequence, then register number and access; a command that passes the sequence rule consumes its number.

questions.text: Does a telemetry-start with the reply count as a command carried out, and what is the telemetry frame count in a status reply?
questions.default: Yes, counted when status OK; frame count is the number of frames held since reset.
questions.reason: The request does not state it.
questions.answer: Not specified for the first part: the spec does not say whether a telemetry-start command counts as carried out. For the second part, the spec gives the status reply's telemetry frame count (16 bit) and says the frame count changes only when a frame is held and only reset clears it. That supports 'frames held since reset', but the spec does not say 'when status OK'.
questions.evidence: Frame sequence and frame count change only when a frame is held and only reset clears them.

questions.text: Is the busy bit set while a packet is being received or a reply is being built?
questions.default: Busy is 1 from the first byte of a packet until its reply is built.
questions.reason: The request does not define busy.
questions.answer: Busy is 1 from the first byte of a packet until its reply is built.

questions.text: Value of TIMEOUT_CYCLES and its use?
questions.default: Supplied by the shell; not used by the endpoint logic.
questions.reason: The request names the parameter without describing it.
questions.answer: TIMEOUT_CYCLES is 100000. The specification does not say how it is used, so the proposed default ('Supplied by the shell; not used by the endpoint logic') is not confirmed by the spec.
